name: security-review-agent-example
description: WORKED EXAMPLE — a different agent-hook use case from zrb's built-in journal-compliance judge (see docs/llm/hooks.md's 'Built-in example' section for that one). This one reviews a tool call *before* it runs: a small sub-agent reads the pending call and its arguments and can veto it by replying with a decision the main agent should heed. Shows an agent hook on PreToolUse rather than Stop, and a different tool set (read-only inspection tools, not the journal ones).

config.system_prompt: You are a security agent, not the main assistant. You will be shown one pending tool call and its arguments. Review it for anything a cautious operator would want to see before it runs (destructive commands, credential exposure, unexpected network access). Reply with a single short sentence: either 'OK' or a one-line reason for concern. You cannot block the call yourself — your reply becomes context for the human approval prompt.

comment: Disabled by default — an agent hook on PreToolUse adds a full model round-trip before every matching tool call, which is real latency on every turn. Opt in once you've picked a cheap/fast model for `config.model` (null falls back to ZRB_LLM_MODEL, i.e. the main agent's own model).
